title: Product Kickoff — Fireflies Clone v2
description: Kickoff for v2: scope, design direction, and milestones.
transcript: 00:04 Vishesh Gupta: Alright, thanks for joining everyone. Today we're officially kicking off v2 of the platform, so let's align on scope, design direction, and the roadmap.
00:22 Priya Sharma: Before we dive in, are we still targeting the October 30th launch date?
00:29 Vishesh Gupta: Yes, October 30th is the plan. That gives us roughly three sprints, so we'll need to be disciplined about scope.
00:41 Arjun Mehta: What's the headline feature set for v2? Is it the new Notepad or the mobile app?
00:49 Vishesh Gupta: Both, actually. The new Notepad layout is the priority — the two-panel view with the summary on the left and transcript on the right. Mobile ships right after.
01:05 Priya Sharma: I've been working on the two-panel layout in Figma. The key change is the collapsible icon rail on the left for smart search, soundbites, and comments.
01:18 Vishesh Gupta: Can you walk us through the main screens?
01:23 Priya Sharma: Sure. There are five core screens: the dashboard, the meetings library, the Notepad detail view, the tasks page, and the settings page. I'll share the Figma link after this call.
01:39 Sneha Rao: What about the interactive transcript? I remember we wanted clicking a line to jump the audio to that moment.
01:48 Vishesh Gupta: That's still the plan. Clicking any transcript line seeks the player to that timestamp, and the active line highlights while audio plays.
02:00 Arjun Mehta: How are we syncing playback with the transcript? Is that a polling approach or event-driven?
02:08 Vishesh Gupta: Event-driven — we subscribe to time updates and use a binary search over the sorted segments to find the active line. It should stay smooth even for hour-long meetings.
02:24 Rahul Verma: On the backend side, I'll design the database schema this week. We're looking at meetings, participants, transcript segments, summaries, and action items as the core tables.
02:39 Vishesh Gupta: Perfect. Rahul, when can you share the schema draft?
02:44 Rahul Verma: I'll have a first draft by Wednesday. I want to get the relationships right — especially how action items link back to the transcript segments they came from.
02:58 Sneha Rao: I have a question about the AI summaries. Are we generating them from the transcripts, or is there a rules engine?
03:09 Vishesh Gupta: Both. We'll ship a rules engine first — keyword extraction, topic detection, that kind of thing — and layer in LLM generation later behind a feature flag.
03:22 Sneha Rao: Got it. I'd love to run some user research on the new summary format before we lock it in.
03:30 Vishesh Gupta: Good idea. Sneha, can you plan three or four interviews next week? We want to validate the summary sections — overview, action items, topics, and metrics.
03:45 Sneha Rao: Absolutely, I'll schedule those for next Tuesday through Thursday and share a research plan by Monday.
03:56 Arjun Mehta: For the engineering side, I'll set up the new repository structure and the CI pipeline. I think we should split it into a Next.js frontend and a FastAPI backend.
04:10 Vishesh Gupta: Yes, let's do that. Two deployables, one repo. Arjun, can you own the frontend scaffolding?
04:19 Arjun Mehta: Sure, I'll have the scaffold with the design tokens ready by Friday.
04:27 Priya Sharma: One thing I want to flag — we should agree on the dark theme palette early, because everything cascades from the tokens.
04:38 Vishesh Gupta: Agreed. Let's use the neutral dark-gray base with purple accents. I'll send the palette reference in Slack today.
04:51 Rahul Verma: What about audio? Do we need real recordings for testing?
04:57 Vishesh Gupta: We'll generate placeholder audio — soft tones per speaker turn — so the player and the transcript sync behave realistically without shipping big files.
05:12 Priya Sharma: That's clever. How do we handle meetings that don't have audio at all?
05:19 Vishesh Gupta: The player falls back to a virtual clock, so seek, speed control, and transcript highlighting still work.
05:31 Arjun Mehta: Nice. That means we can demo the interactive transcript even on scheduled meetings.

05:38 Vishesh Gupta: Exactly. Okay, let's talk milestones. Sprint one is foundations — schema, scaffolding, design tokens, and the app shell. Sprint two is the Notepad. Sprint three is polish, search, and exports.
06:00 Priya Sharma: Will we have a design review before sprint two starts?
06:06 Vishesh Gupta: Yes, I'd like a full walkthrough on October 16th. Everyone should attend, and we'll compare side by side with the reference screenshots.
06:19 Sneha Rao: I'll bring the research findings to that review if the interviews go well.
06:25 Vishesh Gupta: Perfect. Rahul, what's the story with migrations? Are we using Alembic?
06:32 Rahul Verma: Yes, Alembic from day one. A clean baseline migration, and we seed demo data on startup so the app is immediately usable.
06:44 Vishesh Gupta: Love it. One more thing — action items. Let me make sure we're all clear on owners.
06:52 Priya Sharma: I own the Figma screens and the two-panel layout spec. I'll share both by Wednesday.
07:00 Arjun Mehta: I own the repo setup, CI, and the frontend scaffold by Friday.
07:06 Rahul Verma: I own the schema draft by Wednesday and the seeder by Friday.
07:12 Sneha Rao: I own the research plan by Monday and the interviews next week.
07:18 Vishesh Gupta: And I'll align with the stakeholders and send a status update to the leadership channel every Friday. I think that covers it — any blockers?
07:30 Arjun Mehta: No blockers on my end, but I'm curious about the smart search filters. Are those rule-based?
07:38 Vishesh Gupta: Yes, rule-based classification — questions, tasks, dates, metrics, pricing, and sentiment. The filters show counts and jump you into the transcript.
07:52 Priya Sharma: That sounds really useful for sales calls. I can already see the team using the pricing filter every day.
08:01 Vishesh Gupta: Alright, great kickoff everyone. Let's reconvene on Monday for sprint planning. Thanks all!
08:12 Rahul Verma: Thanks everyone. I'll send the schema link to the channel as soon as it's ready.

summary.overview: The team kicked off v2 of the platform, targeting an October 30th launch across three sprints. Core scope covers the new two-panel Notepad, an interactive transcript synced to the player, a rules-based summary engine with LLM support later, and a new neutral dark theme with purple accents. Owners agreed on week-one deliverables: Figma screens, database schema, frontend scaffold, and a research plan.
notes: Launch target is October 30th, structured across three sprints
Notepad redesign is the priority — two-panel layout with a collapsible icon rail
Transcript-player sync uses an event-driven binary search over sorted segments
Summaries ship rule-based first, LLM generation lands later behind a feature flag
Placeholder audio is synthesized per speaker turn; a virtual clock covers meetings without media
Design tokens use a neutral dark-gray base with purple accents, agreed early to avoid rework
Full design review scheduled for October 16th, compared against reference screenshots
